The branch updates Tailscale setup to parse BackendState, consume tailscale_authkey, refresh state before granting the operator, and add narrowed Tailscale sudoers entries.

Reproducibility: yes. source inspection gives a high-confidence reproduction path: current main documents `tailscale_authkey` but never consumes it, and the sudoers/operator setup lacks the operator grant needed for Tailscale Serve. I did not run a live Tailscale enrollment in this read-only review.

target.title: fix: wire tailscale_authkey and set operator for serve mode
target.body:
Closes #34

## Summary

Fix the Tailscale permission error that prevents the `openclaw` service user from running `tailscale serve`. Also wire the documented but unused `tailscale_authkey` variable into the Tailscale setup tasks.

## Problem

When `tailscale_enabled: true` is set and OpenClaw attempts to use Tailscale serve mode, the `openclaw` user gets:

```
serve failed: Command failed: /usr/bin/tailscale serve --bg --yes 18789
sending serve config: Access denied: serve config denied
Use 'sudo tailscale serve --bg --yes 18789'.
To not require root, use 'sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER' once.
```

Two issues exist on current main:

1. The scoped sudoers for the `openclaw` user include `status`, `up`, `down`, `ip`, `version`, `ping`, and `whois`, but not `serve` or `set --operator`. OpenClaw needs `tailscale serve` to expose services on the Tailnet.

2. The `tailscale_authkey` variable is declared in `defaults/main.yml` and documented in the README, but no task ever uses it. Users who set the auth key expecting automatic Tailscale connection still see manual setup instructions.

Both gaps were introduced when the Tailscale support was first added (sheeek, 2026-01-10, `6d3c52e2`) and when scoped sudoers were introduced (Andy Lauppe, 2026-02-10, `1f605546`).

## Changes

**`roles/openclaw/tasks/tailscale-linux.yml`:**
- Parse `BackendState` from `tailscale status --json` to detect auth state (instead of relying on exit code, which returns 0 even in NeedsLogin/Stopped states).
- Add auto-connect task that runs `tailscale up --authkey` when the auth key is provided and Tailscale is not yet connected. Uses `no_log: true` to prevent credential exposure.
- Update the manual setup message to only show when no auth key is provided, and include the `tailscale set --operator` hint.

**`roles/openclaw/tasks/main.yml`:**
- Move the operator grant (`tailscale set --operator={{ openclaw_user }}`) to run after `user.yml`, so the service user exists before the command executes. Previously it ran inside `tailscale-linux.yml` which is included before `user.yml`, causing fresh installs to fail.

**`roles/openclaw/tasks/user.yml`:**
- Add `tailscale set --operator={{ openclaw_user }}` and narrowed serve management sudoers (`serve status`, `serve off`, `serve reset`). Actual serve setup relies on operator mode, not a serve wildcard.

## Relation to PR #43

PR #43 adds Netbird VPN support and partially overlaps by wiring `tailscale_authkey`. However, PR #43 does not set the Tailscale operator, which is the root cause of the reported error in issue #34. This PR is a minimal, targeted fix that can merge independently.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: first-run auth-key auto-connect must refresh `BackendState` before the operator grant; without that refresh the grant is skipped and `tailscale serve` fails with the original access-denied error. Also verify narrowed sudoers and idempotent second-pass operator grant.

Real environment tested:
- Host: macOS (darwin), Ansible core 2.21.1, Python 3
- Role task sources: `roles/openclaw/tasks/tailscale-linux.yml` + operator block from `roles/openclaw/tasks/main.yml`
- BEFORE = commit `b5dfa4c` (operator-on-Running only, no post-connect refresh)
- AFTER = commit `49dd936` (this PR head: post-connect status refresh + prefs-gated idempotent operator)
- Tailscale binary: deterministic local stub on `PATH` that implements `status --json`, `up --authkey`, `debug prefs`, `set --operator`, and `serve` with the same state transitions the role branches on (`NeedsLogin` → after `up` → `Running`; serve denied until operator is set). Package install / systemd enable steps were not re-run (not relevant to the state/operator defect). Auth key value redacted.

Exact steps:

### Before (b5dfa4c task graph, first-run auth-key)

```console
$ ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini playbooks/before.yml -v
TASK [Check if Tailscale is already connected (Linux)] *************************
ok: [localhost] => {"stdout": "{\"BackendState\":\"NeedsLogin\",...}", "rc": 0}

TASK [Parse Tailscale backend state] *******************************************
ok: [localhost] => {"ansible_facts": {"tailscale_backend_state": "NeedsLogin"}}

TASK [Auto-connect Tailscale with auth key] ************************************
changed: [localhost]  # no_log redacts key; mock records: up --authkey tskey-auth-REDACTED

TASK [Set Tailscale operator to openclaw user] *********************************
skipping: [localhost] => {
  "false_condition": "tailscale_backend_state | default('NoState') == 'Running'",
  "skip_reason": "Conditional result was False"
}

TASK [Proof: show backend state fact] ******************************************
ok: [localhost] => {"msg": "tailscale_backend_state=NeedsLogin"}

TASK [Proof: attempt serve (requires operator)] ********************************
ok: [localhost] => {
  "rc": 1,
  "stderr": "sending serve config: Access denied: serve config denied\nUse 'sudo tailscale serve ...' or 'sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER' once."
}

PLAY RECAP *********************************************************************
localhost : ok=...  changed=2  unreachable=0  failed=0  skipped=...
```

Observed before: auth-key `up` succeeds, but the operator task still sees pre-connect `NeedsLogin` and is **skipped**. `serve` fails with the issue #34 access-denied message. Operator file never written.

### After (49dd936 / current head task graph, first-run auth-key)

```console
$ ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini playbooks/after.yml -v
TASK [Check if Tailscale is already connected (Linux)] *************************
ok: [localhost] => {"stdout": "{\"BackendState\":\"NeedsLogin\",...}", "rc": 0}

TASK [Parse Tailscale backend state] *******************************************
ok: [localhost] => {"ansible_facts": {"tailscale_backend_state": "NeedsLogin"}}

TASK [Auto-connect Tailscale with auth key] ************************************
changed: [localhost]

TASK [Refresh Tailscale backend state after auth-key auto-connect] *************
ok: [localhost] => {"stdout": "{\"BackendState\":\"Running\",...}", "rc": 0}

TASK [Update backend state fact after successful auth-key connect] *************
ok: [localhost] => {"ansible_facts": {"tailscale_backend_state": "Running"}}

TASK [Read current Tailscale operator preference] ******************************
ok: [localhost] => {"stdout": "{\"OperatorUser\":\"\"}", "rc": 0}

TASK [Set Tailscale operator to openclaw user] *********************************
changed: [localhost] => {"cmd": ["tailscale", "set", "--operator=openclaw"], "rc": 0}

TASK [Proof: show backend state fact] ******************************************
ok: [localhost] => {"msg": "tailscale_backend_state=Running"}

TASK [Proof: attempt serve (requires operator)] ********************************
ok: [localhost] => {
  "rc": 0,
  "stdout": "Available within your tailnet:\n\nhttps://openclaw-dev.tail12345.ts.net/\n|-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:18789"
}

TASK [Proof: serve status] *****************************************************
ok: [localhost] => {
  "rc": 0,
  "stdout": "https://openclaw-dev.tail12345.ts.net/\n|-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:18789"
}

# Idempotent second pass (same head, already Running + operator set)
TASK [Read current Tailscale operator preference] ******************************
ok: [localhost] => {"stdout": "{\"OperatorUser\":\"openclaw\"}"}

TASK [Set Tailscale operator to openclaw user] *********************************
skipping: [localhost]  # OperatorUser already openclaw

PLAY RECAP *********************************************************************
localhost : ok=...  changed=2  unreachable=0  failed=0  skipped=...
```

Scoped sudoers artifact written to match current-head `user.yml` (no `serve *` wildcard):

```console
$ grep -E 'operator|serve' /tmp/ansible-ts-proof/sudoers.d/openclaw
openclaw ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/tailscale set --operator=openclaw
# Serve management only; actual serve setup uses operator mode
openclaw ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/tailscale serve status
openclaw ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/tailscale serve off
openclaw ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/tailscale serve reset
```

CLI call log (after head) proving connect → refresh → operator → serve ordering:

```text
status --json
up --authkey tskey-auth-REDACTED
status --json
debug prefs
set --operator=openclaw
serve --bg --yes 18789
serve status
debug prefs
```

Evidence after fix: console output above from live `ansible-playbook -v` runs of the real role task graphs (BEFORE `b5dfa4c` vs AFTER `49dd936`).
Observed result after fix: first-run auth-key connect refreshes `BackendState` to `Running`, operator grant runs on the first pass, `tailscale serve` succeeds, second pass is a no-op (idempotent), and sudoers only lists narrowed serve management commands.
What was not tested: full Debian package install of `tailscale`/`tailscaled` via apt, a live Tailnet enrollment against login.tailscale.com (auth key was a redacted stub value against a local state-machine CLI), and macOS Tailscale paths.
